title: The Programme Concession Carried by a Client Who Also Books Events
content:
A client whose events run through Private Event & Banquet Services is carrying the dining programme across two books, and a concession is taken on the value standing on a pulled catering order to answer that.

**Where the client holds a private event and banquet agreement billing under the same client account code as the Corporate Catering Service Agreement, that agreement stands active and the largest guest count its package handles reaches 200**, a programme concession of 4 percentage points — 4.0 per cent — is taken on the value standing.

**Where the client holds such an agreement under that account code that stands active and the largest guest count its package handles falls short of 200**, a programme concession of 2 percentage points — 2.0 per cent — is taken.

**Otherwise**, no programme concession is taken.

### The records read

The agreements are matched by the client account code the catering agreement is written against. Against that account code the client's Private Event & Banquet Services agreement is read for two things: whether it stands active, and the largest guest count the package recorded on it handles.

| Banquet agreement under the same client account code | Largest guest count its package handles | Programme concession |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Stands active | reaches 200 | 4.0 per cent |
| Stands active | falls short of 200 | 2.0 per cent |
| Does not stand active | either way | none |
| No such agreement | — | none |

A package whose largest guest count handled is exactly 200 reaches 200 and carries the concession of 4.0 per cent; one whose largest guest count handled is 199 falls short of 200 and carries 2.0 per cent. A banquet agreement billing under a different client account code from the catering agreement is not matched at all, whatever guest count its package handles.
